reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a live SUSHI price chart with buy and sell indicators, consistent with trading-signal commentary rather than a deceptive solicitation. The visible content does not promise returns or direct viewers to send money or data anywhere; the description asks viewers to make their own decisions.

citations.quote: This stream is for informational purpose only!
Make your own decisions, do your DD on Sushi

opening.argument: Judge the invitation conveyed by the whole presentation, not just whether it says “guaranteed profit.” The stream calls itself “Live Signals” and displays BUY markers on the SUSHI price chart, including beside a subsequent rise. That pairs a suggested action with the prospect of price appreciation, even without an explicit return figure. The instruction to “Make your own decisions” does not remove the trading prompt; it leaves viewers to act on it. The strongest concern is an implied token-buying opportunity, though the record does not show a purchase link or an express profit promise.

citations.quote: Make your own decisions, do your DD on Sushi

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the absence of a payment destination or promised return as decisive. But its own chart evidence includes BUY and SELL markers, while the title offers “Live Signals.” Those are action-oriented cues, not merely a report of past prices. “Make your own decisions” assigns responsibility to the viewer; it does not establish that the signals are neutral.

citations.quote: Make your own decisions, do your DD on Sushi

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A chart marking possible buys and sells is consistent with trading analysis, but it does not establish a deceptive token-purchase solicitation. The sampled frames also show price declines and SELL markers, not a one-way appreciation story. The description explicitly tells viewers to do their own research. There is no evidenced purchase pathway or return claim tying these signals to a scam.

citations.quote: Make your own decisions, do your DD on Sushi

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: a crypto-asset-specific stream titled “Live Signals,” repeated BUY and SELL markers over a moving price chart, and a description that distances the presenter from financial-advice responsibility. The disclaimer matters, but it does not explain how the signals are produced or whether a viewer can rely on them. A judge should be wary of treating that disclaimer as proof that the action cues are harmless. The case for deceptive promotion rests on the combination of actionable-looking signals and limited substantiation, not on an invented guaranteed return.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense says the stream is informational and asks for independent decisions. Yet neither statement verifies the reliability of the prominent trading signals. The chart supplies BUY and SELL cues, and the description simultaneously says that nothing said in the stream should be taken as financial advice. That tension deserves scrutiny rather than automatic acceptance of the disclaimer.

citations.quote: Nothing said by me or anyone in the chat should be taken as financial advice.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Unverified signals are not, by themselves, evidence of deception. The cited frame shows both BUY and SELL markers amid changing prices, and the description cautions viewers to make their own decisions and research Sushi. No supplied material promises easy gains, asks for funds, or shows a mechanism for extracting money or data.

citations.quote: Make your own decisions, do your DD on Sushi

opening.argument: This is framed as information, but its practical focus is participation in SUSHI trading. The title promises “Live Signals,” the chart repeatedly marks BUY and SELL points, and the description directs viewers to do their research “on Sushi.” Those choices keep a particular token and potential trades in view. Calling the stream informational does not settle whether its signals function as promotion; a judge can reasonably read the presentation as steering attention toward buying when the chart indicates it. The evidence supports that promotional reading, even though it does not show a link to buy or a stated gain.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense accurately describes a price chart, but that does not make the stream passive market news. The chart places BUY markers alongside price movement, and the title advertises signals rather than a general market update. The absence of a deposit request narrows the concern; it does not answer whether the presentation steers viewers toward token purchases.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Focusing on one token and showing trading indicators is ordinary market commentary, not sufficient evidence of a scam. The chart includes SELL as well as BUY markers, while the description calls the stream informational and urges independent research. The prosecution's promotional interpretation does not establish a deceptive claim, a promised appreciation, or a purchase pathway.
